narr: A nearly stationary frontal boundary remained across the Saint John Valley from the 27th into the 28th. The front served as a focus for heavy rain with embedded thunderstorms through the overnight hours of the 27th into the morning of the 28th. Along the Saint John Valley of northeast Aroostook county...rainfall totals from the overnight hours of the 27th into the morning of the 28th generally ranged from 3.00 to 4.50 inches with local totals in excess of 5.00 inches. In some areas...2.00 to 3.00 inches of rain fell in less than 4 hours during the early morning hours of the 28th. The heavy rains led to localized flash flooding which persisted into the late morning of the 28th. Several roads were closed due to rapidly flowing water including Little Madawaska Lake Road...Saint Marys Brook Road and West Road. The cemetary was flooded in the town of Van Buren. A beaver dam collapsed...releasing water which had impounded behind the dam. The surge of water from the release overwhelmed a culvert which led to a washout and total collapse of a portion of Route 1 near Cyr Plantation. The road was closed for nearly a month while repairs were completed.
